title: Batch queue hang — heuristic investigation notes
body:
Status / quick summary:
- Intermittent 'batch queue hang' observed on prod serving clusters (us-west-2) across two host pools 2024-10-02 22:30 UTC -> 2024-10-03 03:00 UTC. Symptoms: rising tail latency on generation RPCs, sporadic OOMs on a subset of GPU workers, large microbatch waiting times (head-of-line > 1s) despite average token latencies normal.

Impact:
- ~3% of requests experienced >=1s queuing; 1.2% of hosts hit OOM and restarted (eviction/autoscaler triggered). Customer-facing errors: increased 502s for a small set of customers during the window.

Short context / why this doc exists:
- This is a working scratchpad capturing evidence, quick reproduction hints, interim mitigations, and a proposed runbook snippet. Not final. Keep compact.

Observations (data points):
- Queue depth spike correlates with scheduled ephemeral traffic bursts (batching-profile change) + a background work item that enqueues a no-op flush.
- Metric: serving.batch.microbatch_wait_seconds.p99 rose from 0.02s -> 1.1s in impacted hosts.
- Metric: serving.batch.pending_batches_count increased and did not drain for 10-45s in affected hosts.
- GC and memory growth: python process RSS climbed steadily on stuck hosts before OOM; growth coincided with many partial KV-cache insert attempts logged.
- Logs show repeated lines: "coalescer: found 0 eligible tasks, waiting for timer" interleaved with "flusher: attempting to assemble batch but got empty queue". Suspect tight race between coalescer and flusher logic.
- Recent change (PR 1289) modified the batching flush heuristics and added an optimization to skip assembling batches below a microbatch size threshold; this PR was rolled out to 20% last week.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Timer starvation + skip-assemble optimization -> path where the flusher expects a non-empty queue but the coalescer returns empty due to pre-check, leading to a busy-wait loop that prevents the scheduled flush from running (event loop thread starvation).
2) A KV-cache insertion path is synchronous on the worker thread when batches are empty, causing memory amplification if many small requests flow through the same host.
3) Edge case: tokenization/segmentation producing zero-length microbatches that trigger the skip path incorrectly.
4) Lower probability: GC pause alignment causing multiple threads to wait and batch assembly to get stuck.

Reproduction notes (local / simulated):
- Hard to reproduce end-to-end; however a synthetic load that alternates between a) 1 token requests at 400 rps for 20s and b) idle for 5s reproduces queue depth oscillation in staging when PR 1289 is enabled.
- Steps: deploy PR-1289 build to a 2-node staging pool, run load generator with microbatch knobs: target_batch_size=8, target_latency_ms=5, request_size=1 token. Observe pending_batches_count.
- Add a slight jitter to request arrival times to more closely match prod.

Quick mitigations (hot fixes / on-call actions):
- Rollback PR 1289 rollout from 20% -> 0% (safe rollback path validated).
- Temporary config: set batching.skip_small_batches=false on affected pools (config flag added in runtime v0.21). This reduced occurrences in the short run.
- Emergency scale: add +25% hosts to pools with long queues to absorb partial queues while we investigate.
- If host shows steady microbatch_wait_seconds.p50 > 200ms for >2m, trigger automated host drain (safest short-term).

Suggested runbook snippet (for inclusion in serving-runtime incident playbook):
- Pager triggers: sustained batch.pending_batches_count > 50 and microbatch_wait_seconds.p95 > 500ms for 2m on >= 3 hosts in a pool -> SEV2.
- On-call steps:
  1) Check recent deploys (last 6h) in rollout dashboard (console.redwood.dev -> deployments). Identify PRs touching batching heuristics.
  2) Query metrics: pending_batches_count, microbatch_wait_seconds, worker_rss_bytes, kvcache_inserts_rate.
  3) If PR rollout found: initiate rollback, post status in #sre-runtime Slack and pin link.
  4) If no recent deploy: disable skip_small_batches flag on pool via control-plane UI and watch metrics for 5m.
  5) If hosts remain stuck: schedule immediate host drain and rotate out; escalate to oncall-serviceruntime.
  6) Collect logs: gather coalescer/flusher logs (+30s around event) and upload to incident artifact bucket.
  7) If OOM observed: check coredump artifacts and capture pmap / top samples.

Logs/commands we used during triage (useful quick commands):
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=runtime -c runtime | grep coalescer | tail -n 200
- script to sample metric snapshots: scripts/collect_batch_metrics.sh --hosts host1,host2 --out /tmp/metrics-snapshot.json
- curl -sS \"https://console.redwood.dev/api/rollouts?env=prod\" | jq '.rollouts[] | select(.component==\"batcher\")'

Telemetry gaps that hurt diagnosis: 
- No per-batch assembly trace id in logs (only per-request ids). Hard to join coalescer/flusher activities.
- Missing fine-grained timing histogram for the batch assembly code path (we have overall microbatch_wait but not per-step).

Proposed long-term engineering fixes (owners assigned):
- Add deterministic flush timer fallback: if coalescer returns empty but flusher retries > N within X ms, force a timed-assembly path (owner: Lin Zhao, eng-serving-runtime).
- Add per-assembly trace id to logs and emit an event when a flusher finds empty queue (owner: Maya Thompson, eng-execution).
- Review PR-1289 heuristics and add property-based tests for small-batch behavior (owner: Carlos Rivera, eng-serving-runtime).
- KV-cache insert path: make inserts backgrounded and bounded so synchronous inserts don't amplify memory pressure (owner: Evelyn Park, eng-platform).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there other PRs touching tokenization or request normalization in the same rollout window? Quick scan suggests none but need deeper audit.
- Determine safe default for batching.skip_small_batches across customers; some low-latency customers rely on the optimization. Impact analysis needed.
- Can we add a litmus test in CI that asserts no starvation loop for a range of arrival jitter patterns? (Action: write small harness -> add to pre-merge checks).

Post-incident notes / timeline summary for incident report:
- Root cause likely interplay between new skip_small_batches optimization and event-loop scheduling leading to periodic busy loops and memory amplification.
- Immediate rollback + flag flip reduced incidence to baseline.
- Longer-term work required to make the optimization safe and observable.

Owners & next actions (short term):
- Today: rollback if still rolled out (Ravi) -> status: done on 2024-10-03 01:15 UTC.
- This week: staging repro and automated test (Lin & Maya) -> target complete 2024-10-11.
- Medium term: instrumentation + design changes (Carlos & Evelyn) -> target Q4 2024.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Maybe implement a per-host soft cap on synchronous KV-inserts (circuit-breaker).
- Could we prefer event-based flush vs timer when queue length transitions from 0 -> 1? Edge-case tricky.
- Think about a lightweight watchdog thread that observes batch assembly progress and triggers metrics/alert when stuck.

Artifacts collected:
- metrics snapshot: gs://redwood-incident-artifacts/sre/SRE-2145/metrics-20241003-0030.json
- logs archive: gs://redwood-incident-artifacts/sre/SRE-2145/logs-hostpoolA-20241003.tar.gz
- PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289

References / related tickets:
- JIRA SRE-2145 (incident)
summary: Working notes capturing investigation into intermittent batch queue hang causing tail latency and OOMs; includes reproduction attempts, quick mitigations, runbook draft, and next steps.
